blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A code review finds two helpers: `boolean a(Number amount) { return amount instanceof Runnable; }` and `boolean b(Long id) { return id instanceof Runnable; }`. What does javac do with them?

options.text: It compiles both, since a subclass of either class could implement Runnable and make the test true
options.says: Long is final, so no subclass of it can exist to implement Runnable; javac rejects b

options.text: It rejects both, since neither declared class implements Runnable and so no object of either passes
options.says: an interface test compiles against a non-final class, since a subclass of Number may implement Runnable

options.text: It compiles a and rejects b, since a subclass of Number could implement Runnable while Long is final
options.says: Number is not final, so some object could be both; Long is final and doesn't implement Runnable

options.text: It compiles b and rejects a, since Long is final and fully known while a Number could be any subclass
options.says: being final is what makes b impossible: Long can't gain Runnable, while a Number subclass can

origin.section: The Compiler Rejects a Test That Can Never Be True, Judging Only the Declared Types

questions.stem: A reporting service swaps in new versions of its report classes without a restart. A static cache filled before the swap still holds a report: `cached.getClass().getName()` prints `com.example.Report`, yet `cached instanceof Report` is false in the new code. Why?

options.text: The cached object's class came from the old loader, and a class at run time is its name together with its loader
options.says: at run time a class is its name and its defining loader, so the old Report and the new one are unrelated, even when their bytes are the same

options.text: The cached object's class came from the old class file, and a class at run time is its name together with its bytecode
options.says: the bytecode doesn't decide it: the page's Greeter has the same bytes and is still a different class, because another loader defined it

options.text: The cached object's class has the same name but was unloaded, and instanceof is false for an unloaded class
options.says: the cache still holds the object and hands it out; it fails the test because its class came from another loader

options.text: The cached object's class has the same name but the cache declares Object, and instanceof reads that declared type
options.says: instanceof looks at the class of the object, not the declared type of the variable

origin.section: A Class Is Its Name and the Loader That Defined It

questions.stem: A logging helper does `if (value instanceof Object[]) log(Arrays.toString((Object[]) value)); else log(String.valueOf(value));`. It is called once with a `long[]` of order ids and once with a `Long[]` of order ids. What is logged?

options.text: Both lists of ids, since a long[] and a Long[] are each arrays and so pass the test against Object[]
options.says: a long[] holds no references, so it is an Object but not an Object[]

options.text: Neither list of ids, since a long[] and a Long[] each have their own array class, not Object[]
options.says: a Long[], like the page's String[], is also an Object[]

options.text: Only the Long[] ids, since a long[] stores plain values rather than references and so fails the test
options.says: the long[] holds no references and fails the test, so it goes to String.valueOf; the Long[], like a String[], is an Object[]

options.text: Only the long[] ids, since a Long[] stores objects of its own class Long and so fails the test
options.says: a Long[], like the page's String[], is an Object[]; it is the long[] that fails

origin.section: Arrays Keep Their Element Type at Run Time; Generic Types Lose Their Type Arguments

questions.stem: A request handler reads `Object raw = headers.get("X-Retry-Limit")` for a request that doesn't send that header, then runs `Integer boxed = (Integer) raw; int limit = boxed;`. What happens?

options.text: The cast throws ClassCastException, since the absent value is not an Integer
options.says: a cast lets null through; only a non-null object of the wrong class makes it throw

options.text: The cast throws NullPointerException, since checking the class of the absent value dereferences it
options.says: the cast doesn't dereference null; it passes it on

options.text: The unboxing throws NullPointerException, since the cast passed the absent value on
options.says: (Integer) null is null, and unboxing null into an int throws NullPointerException

options.text: The unboxing throws ClassCastException, since the absent value can't be converted to an int
options.says: the cast already passed null on as an Integer; unboxing it throws NullPointerException

origin.section: instanceof Asks About the Object's Class at Run Time, and null Has None

concepts: A cast lets null through, so a missing value surfaces later, for example as a NullPointerException when it is unboxed.
At run time a class is its name together with the loader that defined it, so an object of a class reloaded by another loader fails instanceof and the cast.
javac rejects an instanceof test or a cast that no object could satisfy, judged from the declared types: two unrelated classes, or a final class and an interface it doesn't implement.
